claim: Tower of London 2026 online tickets start at £37 adult / £18.50 child / £29.50 senior, open Tue–Sat 09:00–17:30 and Sun–Mon 10:00–17:30, with advance online booking recommended to skip Crown Jewels queues.
quote: By booking your ticket and arrival slot online in advance, you can help ensure your visit goes to plan. Booking ahead not only guarantees your preferred time slot but also helps you skip the longest queues, especially for the world-famous Crown Jewels.

claim: Westminster Abbey 2026 admission is £31 adult / £28 concession / £14 child, open Mon–Fri 09:30–15:30 and Sat 09:30–15:00; closed to sightseeing Sundays (services only).
quote: Adults pay £31, adults aged 65+ and students pay £28, children (6-17 years) pay £14, and children aged 0-5 are free... The Abbey is open between 9:30am – 3:30pm (Monday - Friday) and 9:30am – 3:00pm (Saturday).

claim: The full Changing of the Guard at Buckingham Palace now only runs on selected dates (not every Mon/Wed/Fri/Sun); ceremony starts at 11:00, lasts about 45 minutes, and visitors should check the Household Division calendar for confirmed dates.
quote: the full ceremony at Buckingham Palace now happens on selected dates throughout the year (not every Mon/Wed/Fri/Sun as in previous years)... The ceremony takes place at either 11:00am or 15:00pm in the Palace forecourt.

claim: St Paul's Cathedral 2026 sightseeing tickets are £27 adult / £10.50 child including crypt, Dome Galleries and audio guide; open Mon–Sat for sightseeing with last entry 4pm, while attending a service is free.
quote: Tickets are priced at £27 per adult and £10.50 per child with discounts for families, groups and concessions and free tickets for those with a disability... Attending a daily service is free.

claim: London Eye standard online tickets run roughly £29–£35 in 2026 (walk-up around £54), with Fast-Track worth it during July/August/December peak periods to save 30–60 minutes of queueing.
quote: Standard online prices usually begin around £29 to £35, depending on the date and demand. However, walk-up pricing can be around £54... If you're visiting in July, August, December, or any school holiday, the Fast-Track option saves 30 to 60 minutes of queueing.

claim: Tower Bridge Exhibition (with high-level glass-floor walkways and Victorian engine rooms) is open daily 09:30–18:00, last entry 17:00, at roughly £12 adult / £6 child for 2026 with online tickets cheaper than walk-up.
quote: Your ticket includes access to the iconic High-Level Walkways with Glass Floors, the North and South Towers, and the atmospheric Victorian Engine Rooms. Tower Bridge is open daily 9:30am–6pm (last entry 5pm).

claim: Sky Garden offers free timed-entry tickets bookable up to 3 weeks ahead (released Monday mornings), open weekdays 10:00–18:00 and weekends 11:00–21:00, with a 1-hour time limit on entry.
quote: Tickets are currently available to book up to three weeks in advance... Tickets are only valid for the date and time stated on the ticket and have a time limit of 1hr from time of entry.

claim: The Shard's viewing platform sits about 90m higher than Sky Garden (244m vs 155m) and costs £28–£35 per adult, giving a more dramatic 'above the city' view, while Sky Garden delivers a comparable central-London panorama for free.
quote: The most obvious difference is height. The Shard's viewing platform is nearly 90 metres higher than the Sky Garden, and that extra altitude makes a noticeable difference. From The Shard, you look down on the City of London's skyscrapers rather than across at them.

claim: Big Ben/Elizabeth Tower tours cost £55 adult / £35 child (11–17), require climbing 334 steps, last 90 minutes, and tickets are released the second Wednesday of each month at 10:00 and sell out fast; Houses of Parliament tours run Saturdays year-round.
quote: Tickets for tours taking place from 1 August 2026 are £55 for adults and £35 for children aged 11-17. Tickets are released on the second Wednesday of every month at 10:00.

claim: Borough Market is open Wed–Sun 10:00–17:30 (closed Mondays, limited Tue) and is best visited on weekday mornings to avoid heaving weekend crowds, especially in December.
quote: The public market opens at 10.00 am on weekdays and 8.00 am on Saturdays. Full Market hours are Wednesday to Sunday, 10am-5.30pm... for less crowds, it's best to go early morning (10 AM) on weekdays.

claim: Frequently flagged London tourist traps in 2025 include Madame Tussauds, Platform 9¾ at King's Cross, London Dungeon, London Bridge Experience, Sherlock Holmes Museum, SEA Life Aquarium, hop-on hop-off buses, and Harrods — all overpriced for what visitors get.
quote: Madame Tussauds... Overcrowded and noisy space filled with okay-ish wax replicas with high admission ($47+ online, $60+ walk-up)... Platform 9¾ at King's Cross Station... Just a wall with a trolley prop; limited experience unless you're a dedicated Potter fan.

claim: Reddit-driven London folklore directs tourists to Angus Steakhouse as a diversion (the steak was reviewed as 'sad' and 'seasoned with despair'), and Fodor's flags Westminster Bridge, Primrose Hill and the London Eye as overcrowded, overpriced or worth skipping for better-view alternatives like Duck and Waffle.
quote: Angus Steakhouse - A Reddit hoax directing tourists to mediocre food; the steak was recently called 'sad' and 'seasoned with despair.'... The London Eye - Slow, expensive (£29+), and touristy. Alternative: Visit Sushi Samba or Duck and Waffle at Heron Tower for superior views.

claim: Horizon 22 (58th floor of 22 Bishopsgate) is the highest free viewing platform in London, fully enclosed with unobstructed views and requires a free timed ticket; Garden at 120 is London's largest public rooftop with wisteria and is also free.
quote: Horizon 22 is the highest free viewing platform in London on the 58th floor of 22 Bishopsgate... Garden at 120 is located right down the street from the Sky Garden at 120 Fenchurch Street and is London's largest public rooftop space.
